new_tests_written_this_session.rationale: Closes an HTTP-contract gap: existing coverage tested submitSecretsFanOut() at the service layer and secretName/jiraTicket validators at the route layer, but no test exercised POST /api/secrets' environments[] handling (mutual exclusivity, duplicates, cap, partial-failure status selection, exhaustive error-code mapping, legacy field preservation, audit log fields) through the real validator chain.
scenarios: all environments succeed -> 201, results[] has one entry per env, no top-level prNumber for a genuine multi-result batch
partial success (2/3) -> 207, success:false, results[] identifies each outcome, no top-level error field
all fail, same errorCode (CONFLICT) -> 503 uniform status
all fail, mixed errorCodes (FOUND_FALSE + CONFLICT) -> 500 fallback, results[] retains each specific code

exhaustive FR-005(c) errorCode -> HTTP status table for all 9 codes (FOUND_FALSE, VAULT_AMBIGUOUS, VAULT_INVALID, PR_EXISTS, CONFLICT, ENCRYPTION_FAILED, SOPS_NOT_CONFIGURED, QUALIFIER_AMBIGUOUS, QUALIFIER_MISMATCH), single-environment fan-out path
legacy singular `environment` success keeps top-level prNumber/prUrl/secretCount alongside results[] (FR-006(a)/(b))
single-element `environments` array gets the same legacy top-level fields as singular shape (FR-006(b))
failed legacy singular `environment` request keeps existing top-level error shape, no regression

design_notes: FR-007's confirmation gate is enforced client-side only, by explicit PRD design (Non-Goals: 'Building a stricter (typed) confirmation pattern' is out of scope; OQ-002 resolution states the portal step's job is preventing accidental selection, with the Jira ticket + human-reviewed PR/merge gate as the actual control). The backend does not reject a request lacking `confirmedProductionWrite: true` for a production-tier environment — it only records the claim for NFR-SEC-002's audit trail. This matches the PRD's explicit governance decision and is not a defect.
